A 22-year-old man visits his primary care provider reporting dysuria and urethral discharge for the past
week. He reports having had unprotected sexual contact with both male and female partners within the
last month. He has no fever or previous episodes of discharge. His medical history is unremarkable
except for occasional alcohol consumption and past marijuana use. He takes no regular medications.
Physical examination reveals normal vital signs (temperature 97.1°F, blood pressure 108/73 mmHg,
pulse 73/min, respiratory rate 12/min). Genital examination shows a circumcised penis with normal
meatal position and non-tender descended testes bilaterally. Laboratory testing reveals large leukocyte
esterase on urinalysis, while urethral swab gram stain is negative. What organism is most likely
responsible for this clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Candida albicans (B) Gardnerella
vaginalis (C) Ureaplasma urealyticum (D) Treponema pallidum (E) Klebsiella granulomatis (F)
Trichomonas vaginalis (G) Haemophilus ducreyi (H) Neisseria gonorrhea (I) Mycoplasma genitalium (J)
Chlamydia trachomatis
 A. Chlamydia trachomatis
